newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher in all months.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher in all months.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher in all months on Monday due to buying from local investors who were encouraged by the stronger Chicago market, traders said.
Prices ranged from 140 yen to 280 yen per tonne higher, with the benchmark May 1998 contract closing 140 yen up at 14,400 yen. The day's estimated trade volume was 45,091 lots.
All months gained from the opening on technical buying from local investors, traders said.
Some months retreated by late morning, but bullish sentiment prevailed throughout the day, they said.
"The rally in the Chicago market on Friday encouraged investors," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.73 per bushel at 0745 GMT, up from $2.70-3/4 at Friday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.86-3/4 a bushel at 0745 GMT, against $8.80-1/2 at Friday's close.
